problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>3$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=2,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{2s-3}{{s}^{2}-3s},\,s>3.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$

feedback.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>4$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=6,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{6s-10}{{s}^{2}-2s-8},\,s>4.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{6s-10}{{s}^{2}-2s-8}-6 \\  & =\frac{s(6s-10)-6({s}^{2}-2s-8)}{{s}^{2}-2s-8} \\  & =\frac{2s+48}{{s}^{2}-2s-8}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>4.$
